instruction: Create a bar chart showing the 2020 monthly food bills (column G, rows 20-31) with months as categories.

metadata.explanation: Task requires: (1) selecting 2020 food bill data (A20:G31), (2) inserting a chart, (3) configuring it as a bar chart with months as x-axis. Evaluator checks if the worksheet contains at least one chart. Similar to original task which creates column charts from cost data.
metadata.scoring_breakdown: 1.0 if at least one chart exists in the worksheet, 0.0 otherwise

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly extracts comprehensive chart properties: chart type via chart.type, data ranges via series.val, category ranges via series.cat (calc.py:67-92)
Metric correctly verifies chart type is bar/column chart using keyword matching (calc.py:53: 'bar' or 'col' in chart_type)
Metric correctly verifies data range includes G20:G31 using regex patterns that handle various cell reference formats ($G$20:$G$31, Sheet.G20:G31) (calc.py:58-74)
Metric correctly verifies category ranges span rows 20-31, corresponding to 12 monthly values (calc.py:76-90)
Expected parameter handling is CORRECT: metric accesses expected_state.get('has_chart') directly, not expected_state.get('rules') (calc.py:26)
Postconfig appropriately saves file with Ctrl+S before verification to ensure chart is persisted (task JSON lines 44-53)
Minor limitation: Does not verify semantic label '2020 food bills' in chart title/legend, but this is mitigated by task setup which loads specific data file where G20:G31 ARE the 2020 food bills
Category range validation is appropriately lenient (line 89 accepts if data range correct even if categories uncertain), avoiding false negatives while maintaining data range accuracy
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Optional enhancement: Could verify chart title or legend contains '2020' or 'food' keywords to ensure semantic context, though current verification is sufficient given controlled task setup
Optional enhancement: Could verify exact category count is 12 (monthly data) if category_ranges extraction is reliable across different chart configurations
